title: Staged traffic debouncer for SLO-triggering and rollback hysteresis
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: Frequent flapping of rollback decisions during early-stage canaries and A/B tests causes noisy rollouts and false positives, especially for low-volume cohorts. We need an automated trigger that is robust to short-lived spikes in latency/error/token-cost and that gracefully suppresses premature rollbacks while still guaranteeing safety for high-severity failures.

Proposal: Implement a "staged traffic debouncer" service which sits inside the rollout decision pipeline. Key features: 1) Multi-signal fusion: combine latency p95/p99 drift, error rate, token-cost-per-request, and throughput drop using weighted scoring. 2) Hysteresis windows: require a sustained violation over a configurable trailing window and a minimum traffic-volume threshold before triggering. 3) Confidence-aware thresholds: compute dynamic thresholds using historical baselines per cohort and Bayesian posterior intervals to avoid triggering on noisy estimates. 4) Emergency short-circuit: immediate abort for catastrophic signals (e.g., catastrophic error rate > 20% or large safety flags) bypasses debounce. 5) Shadow probe integration: optionally escalate when shadow traffic and canary disagree persistently. 6) Traffic-aware smoothing: use exponential smoothing on throughput and token-rate signals to avoid transient resource bursts causing rollbacks. 7) Rollback suppression/backoff: exponential backoff on automatic rollback attempts for the same model/version to prevent oscillation.

Design notes: - The debouncer will export a deterministic score and state for each rollout step so Console and alerts can surface why a decision was made. - Small cohorts (< 200 requests over 10m) use pooled baselining and higher-confidence priors. - Thresholds are expressed per-signal and as a composite score; runbook maps composite score bands to actions (no-op, throttle traffic, pause rollout, immediate rollback). - Integrate with existing rollout controller (canary/A-B/shadow) via a single decision API that returns decision + reason + diagnostic snapshot.

Operational controls and knobs: - Configurable trailing window (default 5m/15m/60m), minimum request floor, smoothing alpha, composite weights, bayesian prior strength, emergency thresholds, and max-auto-retry-per-release. - Audit logs with request-level anchors for postmortem. - Read-only dashboard surfaces the composite score, individual signal contributions, confidence intervals, and cohort volumes.

Acceptance criteria: - New API endpoint validates and scores simulated canary traces. - In offline experiments with historical rollout replays, false positive rollback rate drops >= 65% without increasing time-to-detect for high-impact failures (>1% error uplift) by more than 20%. - Dashboard shows decider state with reasons. - Integration tests with rollout controller covering emergency short-circuit and backoff behavior.

Related artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Staged+Traffic+Debouncer, Experiments notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/rl-debouncer, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2319, On-call runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Debouncer+Runbook
comments: 2026-02-21 - Priya Patel: Kickoff sync with reliability and runtime teams. Agreed to prototype scoring in Python and run against Jan-Feb rollout traces.
2026-02-28 - Marco Rivera: Data engineering provided aggregated cohort metrics for 2025 Q4 and 2026 Q1. Observed high variance for low-volume cohorts — will use pooled priors by default.

2026-03-03 - Evan Liu: Initial prototype implemented: composite score = 0.5*latency_score + 0.3*error_score + 0.2*cost_score. Running replay tests now. Added emergency short-circuit rule to bypass debounce for error_rate > 20%.

2026-03-06 - QA - Sasha Morgan: Replay results: false positive rollback rate reduced 72% on our backlog of 47 canaries. Some misses when throughput drops slowly over 90 minutes — added longer trailing-window experiments.

2026-03-09 - Security - Aisha Thompson: Security review requested for decision API auth and audit log retention. Raised minor concerns about exposing model IDs in dashboards; recommend RBAC controls (implemented in design).

2026-03-10 - Evan Liu: Merged initial feature branch to feature/runtime-debouncer. Next: integrate decision API with rollout controller, add dashboard panels, and run staged rollout in staging with a small set of internal models.
